name: corrections-033
prompt:
Create ORIGINAL FORMA fitness-manual illustrations: THREE columns TWO rows SIX separate equal panels, landscape1536x1024. Fully clothed varied adults, charcoal-gray with lime accents, white background, no text/logos/watermarks. Anatomically correct and physically plausible. Complete whole figures/apparatus inside each panel with generous margins. ONE precise working pose per panel. Follow full actual guide, explicitly correct prior rejected image errors.

Row 1 column 1: Stiff Leg Barbell Good Morning. PRIOR ERROR, DO NOT REPEAT: Good morning stops well above the parallel-torso position described.. Actual full guide: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.

Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance. Keep your head up at all times as looking down will get you off balance and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Keeping your legs stationary, move your torso forward by bending at the hips while inhaling. Lower your torso until it is parallel with the floor.

Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by elevating your torso back to the starting position.

Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Row 1 column 2: Straight-Arm Dumbbell Pullover. PRIOR ERROR, DO NOT REPEAT: Cross-bench pullover hips remain level with the bench rather than below it.. Actual full guide: Place a dumbbell standing up on a flat bench.

Ensuring that the dumbbell stays securely placed at the top of the bench, lie perpendicular to the bench (torso across it as in forming a cross) with only your shoulders lying on the surface. Hips should be below the bench and legs bent with feet firmly on the floor. The head will be off the bench as well.

Grasp the dumbbell with both hands and hold it straight over your chest at arms length. Both palms should be pressing against the underside one of the sides of the dumbbell. This will be your starting position. Caution: Always ensure that the dumbbell used for this exercise is secure. Using a dumbbell with loose plates can result in the dumbbell falling apart and falling on your face.

While keeping your arms straight, lower the weight slowly in an arc behind your head while breathing in until you feel a stretch on the chest.

At that point, bring the dumbbell back to the starting position using the arc through which the weight was lowered and exhale as you perform this movement.

Hold the weight on the initial position for a second and repeat the motion for the prescribed number of repetitions.

Row 1 column 3: Supine Hip Abduction. PRIOR ERROR, DO NOT REPEAT: Supine abduction adds an ankle weight absent from the unweighted guide.. Actual full guide: * **Starting Position:** Lie on your back (supine) on a mat, with your legs extended and relaxed. Arms can be placed alongside your body or out to the sides for stability. * **The Movement:** Slightly lift one leg off the floor (keeping it straight or with a slight bend). Move it laterally outward, away from the other leg, as if stepping over a small obstacle. * **Range of Motion:** Move the leg as far as comfortable without lifting your pelvis or rotating your torso, feeling a stretch in the inner thigh and hip. * **Return:** Slowly bring the leg back to the starting position with controlled movement. * **Goal:** Improves lateral hip mobility (abduction) and strengthens the pelvic stabilizer muscles.

Row 2 column 1: Svend Press. PRIOR ERROR, DO NOT REPEAT: Hands appear to grasp the plate rims rather than pressing the flat plate faces together.. Actual full guide: Begin in a standing position.

Press two lightweight plates together with your hands. Hold the plates together close to your chest to create an isometric contraction in your chest muscles. Your fingers should be pointed forward. This is your starting position.

Squeeze the plates between your palms and extend your arms directly out in front of you in a controlled motion.

Pause at the top of the motion, and then slowly return to the starting position.

Row 2 column 2: Thruster. PRIOR ERROR, DO NOT REPEAT: Overhead bar is received in a deep squat rather than pressed at the standing top of the thruster.. Actual full guide: 1. Start by doing a front squat 2. At the top position, push the bar above your head (similar to a press) 3. Lower the bar to the shoulders

Row 2 column 3: Tibialis raises. PRIOR ERROR, DO NOT REPEAT: Figure rises onto forefeet; tibialis guide requires toes lifted with heels grounded.. Actual full guide: 1. Stand up straight 2. Lift the balls of your feet, resting on your heels.
